notes.title: Problem Set 6 Geometry 10th Standard Maths Part 2 Chapter 6 Trigonometry
notes.content:
Balbharti [Maharashtra State Board Class 10 Maths Solutions](https://maharashtraboardsolutions.com/maharashtra-state-board-class-10-maths-solutions/) covers the Problem Set 6 Geometry 10th Class Maths Part 2 Answers Solutions Chapter 6 Trigonometry.

### Class 10 Maths Part 2 Problem Set 6 Chapter 6 Trigonometry Questions With Answers Maharashtra Board

Question 1.

 Choose the correct alternative answer for the following questions.

i. sin θ.cosec θ = ?

 (A) 1

 (B) 0

 (C) 1 2

 (D) 2–√

 Answer:

 (A)

ii. cosec 45° = ?

 (A) 1 2√

 (B) 2–√

 (C) 3√2

 (D) 1 3√

 Answer:

 (B)

iii. 1 + tan 2 θ = ?

 (A) cot 2 θ

 (B) cosec 2 θ

 (C) sec 2 θ

 (D) tan 2 θ

 Answer:

 (C)

iv. When we see at a higher level, from the horizontal line, angle formed is ______

 (A) angle of elevation.

 (B) angle of depression.

 (C) 0

 (D) straight angle.

 Answer:

 (A)

Question 2.

 If sin θ = 11 61, find the value of cos θ using trigonometric identity.

 Solution:

 sin θ = 11 61 … [Given]

 We know that,

 sin 2 θ + cos 2 θ = 1

![Image 3: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 6 Trigonometry Problem Set 6 1](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-6-Trigonometry-Problem-Set-6-1.png?resize=208%2C93&ssl=1)

![Image 4: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 6 Trigonometry Problem Set 6 2](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-6-Trigonometry-Problem-Set-6-2.png?resize=274%2C172&ssl=1)

 …[Taking square root of both sides]

Question 3.

 If tan θ = 2, find the values of other trigonometric ratios.

 Solution:

 tan θ = 2 …[Given]

 We know that,

 1 + tan 2 θ = sec 7 θ

 ∴ 1 + (2)7 = sec 7 θ

 ∴ 1 + 4 = sec 7 θ

 ∴ sec 7 θ = 5

 ∴ sec θ = 5–√ …[Taking square root of both sides]

![Image 5: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 6 Trigonometry Problem Set 6 3](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-6-Trigonometry-Problem-Set-6-3.png?resize=388%2C536&ssl=1)

Question 4.

 If sec θ = 13 12, find the values of other trigonometric ratios.

 Solution:

 sec θ = 13 12 … [Given]

 We know that,

 1 + tan 2 θ = sec 2 θ

![Image 6: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 6 Trigonometry Problem Set 6 4](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-6-Trigonometry-Problem-Set-6-4.png?resize=388%2C413&ssl=1)

![Image 7: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 6 Trigonometry Problem Set 6 5](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-6-Trigonometry-Problem-Set-6-5.png?resize=384%2C365&ssl=1)

 ∴ sin θ = 5 13, cos θ = 12 13, tan θ = 5 12, cot θ = 12 5, cosec θ = 13 5

Question 5.

 Prove the following:

 i. sec θ (1 – sin θ) (sec θ + tan θ) = 1

 ii. (sec θ + tan θ) (1 – sin θ) = cos θ

 iii. sec 2 θ + cosec 2 θ = sec 2 θ × cosec 2 θ

 iv. cot 2 θ – tan 2 θ = cosec 2 θ – sec 2 θ

 v. tan 4 θ + tan 2 θ = sec 4 θ – sec 2 θ

 vi. 1 1−sin θ+1 1+sin θ = 2 sec2 θ

 vii. sec 6 x – tan 6 x = 1 + 3 sec 2 x × tan 2 x

![Image 8: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 6 Trigonometry Problem Set 6 6](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-6-Trigonometry-Problem-Set-6-6.png?resize=336%2C150&ssl=1)

 Proof:

 i. L.H.S. = sec θ (1 – sin θ) (sec θ + tan θ)

![Image 9: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 6 Trigonometry Problem Set 6 7](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-6-Trigonometry-Problem-Set-6-7.png?resize=328%2C248&ssl=1)

 ∴ sec θ (1 – sin θ) (sec θ + tan θ) = 1

ii. L.H.S. = (sec θ + tan θ) (1 – sin θ)

![Image 10: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 6 Trigonometry Problem Set 6 8](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-6-Trigonometry-Problem-Set-6-8.png?resize=321%2C255&ssl=1)

 ∴ (sec θ + tan θ) (1 – sin θ) = cos θ

iii. L.H.S. = sec 2 θ + cosec 2 θ

![Image 11: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 6 Trigonometry Problem Set 6 9](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-6-Trigonometry-Problem-Set-6-9.png?resize=343%2C228&ssl=1)

 ∴ sec 2 θ + cosec 2 θ = sec 2 θ × cosec 2 θ

iv. L.H.S. = cot 2 θ – tan 2 θ

 = (cosec 2 θ – 1) – (sec 2 θ – 1)

 [∵ tan 2 θ = sec 2 θ – 1,

 cot 2 θ = cosec 2 θ – 1]

 = cosec 2 θ – 1 – sec 2 θ + 1

 cosec 2 θ – sec 2 θ

 = R.H.S.

 ∴ cot 2 θ – tan 2 θ = cosec 2 θ – sec 2 θ

v. L.H.S. = tan 4 θ + tan 2 θ

 = tan 2 θ (tan 2 θ + 1)

 = tan 2 θ. sec 2 θ

 …[∵ 1 + tan 2 θ = sec 2 θ]

 = (sec 2 θ – 1) sec 2 θ

 …[∵ tan 2 θ = sec 2 θ – 1]

 = sec 4 θ – sec 2 θ

 = R.H.S.

 ∴ tan 4 θ + tan 2 θ = sec 4 θ – sec 2 θ

![Image 12: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 6 Trigonometry Problem Set 6 10](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-6-Trigonometry-Problem-Set-6-10.png?resize=377%2C379&ssl=1)

vii. L.H.S. = sec 6 x – tan 6 x

 = (sec 2 x)3 – tan 6 x

 = (1 + tan 2 x)3 – tan 6 x …[∵ 1 + tan 2 θ = sec 2 θ]

 = 1 + 3tan 2 x + 3(tan 2 x)2 + (tan 2 x)3 – tan 6 x …[∵ (a + b)3 = a 3 + 3a 2 b + 3ab 2 + b 3]

 = 1 + 3 tan 2 x (1 + tan 2 x) + tan 6 x – tan 6 x

 = 1 + 3 tan 2 x sec 2 x …[∵ 1 + tan 2 θ = sec 2 θ]

 = R.H.S.

 ∴ sec 3 x – tan 6 x = 1 + 3sec 2 x.tan 2 x

![Image 13: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 6 Trigonometry Problem Set 6 11](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-6-Trigonometry-Problem-Set-6-11.png?resize=390%2C442&ssl=1)

![Image 14: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 6 Trigonometry Problem Set 6 12](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-6-Trigonometry-Problem-Set-6-12.png?resize=387%2C338&ssl=1)

 x. We know that,

 sin 2 θ + cos 2 θ = 1

 ∴ 1 – sin 2 θ = cos 2 θ

 ∴ (1 – sin θ) (1 + sin θ) = cos θ. cos θ

![Image 15: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 6 Trigonometry Problem Set 6 13](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-6-Trigonometry-Problem-Set-6-13.png?resize=350%2C227&ssl=1)

![Image 16: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 6 Trigonometry Problem Set 6 14](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-6-Trigonometry-Problem-Set-6-14.png?resize=376%2C542&ssl=1)

![Image 17: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 6 Trigonometry Problem Set 6 15](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-6-Trigonometry-Problem-Set-6-15.png?resize=383%2C608&ssl=1)

Question 6.

 A boy standing at a distance of 48 metres from a building observes the top of the building and makes an angle of elevation of 30°. Find the height of the building.

 Solution:

 Let AB represent the height of the building and point C represent the position of the boy.

 Angle of elevation = ∠ACB = 30°

 BC = 48 m

![Image 18: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 6 Trigonometry Problem Set 6 16](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-6-Trigonometry-Problem-Set-6-16.png?resize=138%2C145&ssl=1)

 In right angled ∆ABC,

 tan 30° = A B B C … [By definition]

![Image 19: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 6 Trigonometry Problem Set 6 17](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-6-Trigonometry-Problem-Set-6-17.png?resize=346%2C217&ssl=1)

 ∴ The height of the building is 16 3–√ m.

Question 7.

 From the top of the lighthouse, an observer looks at a ship and finds the angle of depression to be 30°. If the height of the lighthouse is 100 metres, then find how far the ship is from the lighthouse.

 Solution:

 Let AB represent the height of lighthouse and point C represent the position of the ship.

![Image 20: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 6 Trigonometry Problem Set 6 18](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-6-Trigonometry-Problem-Set-6-18.png?resize=174%2C171&ssl=1)

 Angle of depression ∠PAC 30°

 AB = 100m.

 Now, ray AP || seg BC

 ∴ ∠ACB = ∠PAC … [Alternate angles]

 ∴ ∠ACB = 30°

 AB = 100m

 In right angled ∆ABC,

 tan 30° = A B B C …[By definition]

 ∴ 1 3√=100 B C

 ∴ BC = 100 3–√m

 ∴ The ship is 1oo 3–√m far from the lighthouse.

Question 8.

 Two buildings are in front of each other on a road of width 15 metres. From the top of the first building, having a height of 12 metre, the angle of elevation of the top of the second building is 30°. What is the height of the second building?

 Solution:

 Let AB and CD represent the heights of the two buildings, and BD represent the width of the road.

![Image 21: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 6 Trigonometry Problem Set 6 19](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-6-Trigonometry-Problem-Set-6-19.png?resize=186%2C210&ssl=1)

 Draw seg AM ⊥ seg CD

 Angle of elevation = ∠CAM = 30°

 AB = 12m

 BD = 15m

 In ꠸ ABDM,

 ∠B = ∠D = 90°

 ∠M 90° …[segAM ⊥ segCD]

 ∠A 90° …[Remaining angle of ꠸ABDM]

 ꠸ABDM is a rectangle …[Each angle is 90°]

![Image 22: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 6 Trigonometry Problem Set 6 20](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-6-Trigonometry-Problem-Set-6-20.png?resize=371%2C397&ssl=1)

 ∴ The height of the second building is 20.65 m.

Question 9.

 A ladder on the platform of a fire brigade van can be elevated at an angle of 70° to the maximum. The length of the ladder can be extended upto 20 m. If the platform is 2 m above the ground, find the maximum height from the ground upto which the ladder can reach. (sin 70° = 0.94)

 Solution:

 Let AB represent the length of the ladder and AE represent the height of the platform.

![Image 23: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 6 Trigonometry Problem Set 6 21](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-6-Trigonometry-Problem-Set-6-21.png?resize=156%2C144&ssl=1)

 Draw seg AC ⊥ seg BD.

 Angle of elevation = ∠BAC = 70°

 AB = 20 m

 AE = 2m

 In right angled ∆ABC,

 sin 70° = B C A B …..[By definition]

 ∴ 0.94 = B C 20

 ∴ BC = 0.94 × 20

 = 18.80 m

 In ꠸ACDE,

 ∠E = ∠D = 90°

 ∠C = 90° … [seg AC ⊥ seg BD]

 ∴ ∠A = 90° … [Remaining angle of ꠸ACDE]

 ∴ ꠸ACDE is a rectangle. … [Each angle is 90°]

 ∴ CD = AE = 2 m … [Opposite sides of a rectangle]

 Now, BD = BC + CD … [B – C – D]

 = 18.80 + 2

 = 20.80 m

 ∴ The maximum height from the ground upto which the ladder can reach is 20.80 metres.

Question 10.

 While landing at an airport, a pilot made an angle of depression of 20°. Average speed of the plane was 200 km/hr. The plane reached the ground after 54 seconds. Find the height at which the plane was when it started landing, (sin 20° = 0.342)

 Solution:

 Let AC represent the initial height and point A represent the initial position of the plane.

 Let point B represent the position where plane lands.

 Angle of depression = ∠EAB = 20°

![Image 24: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 6 Trigonometry Problem Set 6 22](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-6-Trigonometry-Problem-Set-6-22.png?resize=190%2C124&ssl=1)

 Now, seg AE || seg BC

 ∴ ∠ABC = ∠EAB … [Alternate angles]

 ∴ ∠ABC = 20°

 Speed of the plane = 200 km/hr

 = 200 × 1000 3600 m/sec

 = 500 9 m/sec

 ∴ Distance travelled in 54 sec = speed × time

 = 500 9 × 54

 = 3000 m

 ∴ AB = 3000 m

 In right angled ∆ABC,

 sin 20° = A C A B ….[By definition]

 ∴ 0.342 = A C 3000

 ∴ AC = 0.342 × 3000

 = 1026 m

 ∴ The plane was at a height of 1026 m when it started landing.

notes.title: Practice Set 7.2 Geometry 10th Standard Maths Part 2 Chapter 7 Mensuration
notes.content:
Balbharti [Maharashtra State Board Class 10 Maths Solutions](https://maharashtraboardsolutions.com/maharashtra-state-board-class-10-maths-solutions/) covers the Practice Set 7.2 Geometry 10th Class Maths Part 2 Answers Solutions Chapter 7 Mensuration.

### Class 10 Maths Part 2 Practice Set 7.2 Chapter 7 Mensuration Questions With Answers Maharashtra Board

Question 1.

 The radii of two circular ends of frustum shaped bucket are 14 cm and 7 cm. Height of the bucket is 30 cm. How many litres of water it can hold? (1 litre = 1000 cm 3)

 Given: Radii (r 1) = 14 cm, and (r 2) = 7 cm,

 height (h) = 30 cm

 To find: Amount of water the bucket can hold.

 Solution:

 Volume of frustum = 1 3 πh (r 1 2 + r 2 2 + r 1 × r 2)

![Image 3: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 7 Mensuration Practice Set 7.2 1](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-7-Mensuration-Practice-Set-7.2-1.png?resize=338%2C235&ssl=1)

 ∴ The bucket can hold 10.78 litres of water.

Question 2.

 The radii of ends of a frustum are 14 cm and 6 cm respectively and its height is 6 cm. Find its

 i. curved surface area,

 ii. total surface area,

 iii. volume, (π = 3.14)

 Given: Radii (r 1) = 14 cm, and (r 2) = 6 cm,

 height (h) = 6 cm

 Solution:

![Image 4: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 7 Mensuration Practice Set 7.2 2](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-7-Mensuration-Practice-Set-7.2-2.png?resize=315%2C153&ssl=1)

 i. Curved surface area of frustum

 = πl (r 1 + r 2)

 = 3.14 × 10(14 + 6)

 = 3.14 × 10 × 20 = 628 cm 2

 ∴ The curved surface area of the frustum is 628 cm 2.

ii. Total surface area of frustum

 = πl (r 1+ r 2) + πr 1 2 + πr 2 2

 = 628 + 3.14 × (14)2 + 3.14 × (6)2

 = 628 + 3.14 × 196 + 3.14 × 36

 = 628 + 3.14(196 + 36)

 = 628 + 3.14 × 232

 = 628 + 728.48

 = 1356.48 cm 2

 ∴ The total surface area of the frustum is 1356.48 cm 2.

iii. Volume of frustum

 = 1 3 πth(r 1 2 +r 2 2 + r 1 × r 2)

 = 1 3 × 3.14 × 6(14 2 + 6 2 + 14 × 6)

 = 3.14 × 2(196 + 36 + 84)

 = 3.14 × 2 × 316

 = 1984.48 cm 3

 ∴ The volume of the frustum is 1984.48 cm 3.

Question 3.

 The circumferences of circular faces of a frustum are 132 cm and 88 cm and its height is 24 cm. To find the curved surface area of frustum, complete the following activity. (π = 22 7)

 Solution:

 Circumference1 = 27πr 1= 132 cm

![Image 5: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 7 Mensuration Practice Set 7.2 3](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-7-Mensuration-Practice-Set-7.2-3.png?resize=369%2C310&ssl=1)

 Curved surface area of frustum = π (r 1 + r 2) l

 = π (21 + 14) × 25

 =π × 35 × 35

 = 22 7 × 35 × 25

 = 2750 cm 2

notes.title: Practice Set 7.3 Geometry 10th Standard Maths Part 2 Chapter 7 Mensuration
notes.content:
Balbharti [Maharashtra State Board Class 10 Maths Solutions](https://maharashtraboardsolutions.com/maharashtra-state-board-class-10-maths-solutions/) covers the Practice Set 7.3 Geometry 10th Class Maths Part 2 Answers Solutions Chapter 7 Mensuration.

### Class 10 Maths Part 2 Practice Set 7.3 Chapter 7 Mensuration Questions With Answers Maharashtra Board

Practice Set 7.3 Geometry Class 10 Question 1.

 Radius of a circle is 10 cm. Measure of an arc of the circle is 54°. Find the area of the sector associated with the arc. (π = 3.14)

 Given : Radius (r) = 10 cm,

 Measure of the arc (θ) = 54°

 To find : Area of the sector.

 Solution:

 Area of sector = \(\frac{\theta}{360} \times \pi r^{2}\)

 = \(\frac { 54 }{ 360 } \) × 3.14 × (10)2

 = \(\frac { 3 }{ 20 } \) × 3.14 × 100

 = 3 × 3.14 × 5

 = 15 × 3.14

 = 47.1 cm 2

 ∴ The area of the sector is 47.1 cm 2.

Mensuration Practice Set 7.3 Question 2.

 Measure of an arc of a circle is 80° and its radius is 18 cm. Find the length of the arc. (π = 3.14)

 Given: Radius (r) = 18 cm,

 Measure of the arc (θ) = 80°

 To find: Length of the arc.

 Solution:

 Length of arc = \(\frac{\theta}{360} \times 2 \pi r\) × 2πr

 = \(\frac { 8 }{ 360 } \) × 2 × 3.14 × 18

 = \(\frac { 2 }{ 9 } \) × 2 × 3.14 × 18

 = 2 × 2 × 3.14 × 2 = 25.12 cm

 ∴ The length of the arc is 25.12 cm.

Practice Set 7.3 Geometry Question 3.

 Radius of a sector of a circle is 3.5 cm and length of its arc is 2.2 cm. Find the area of the sector.

 Solution:

 Given: Radius (r) = 3.5 cm,

 length of arc (l) = 2.2 cm

 To find: Area of the sector.

 Solution:

 Area of sector = \(\frac{l \times \mathrm{r}}{2}\)

 = \(\frac{2.2 \times 3.5}{2}\)

 = 1.1 × 3.5 = 3.85 cm 2

 ∴ The area of the sector is 3.85 cm 2.

Question 4.

 Radius of a circle is 10 cm. Area of a sector of the circle is 100 cm 2. Find the area of its corresponding major sector, (π = 3.14)

 Given: Radius (r) = 10 cm,

 area of minor sector =100 cm 2

 To find: Area of maj or sector.

 Solution:

 Area of circle = πr 2

 = 3.14 × (10)2

 = 3.14 × 100 = 314 cm 2

 Now, area of major sector

 = area of circle – area of minor sector

 = 314 – 100

 = 214 cm 2

 ∴ The area of the corresponding major sector is 214 cm 2.

Question 5.

 Area of a sector of a circle of radius 15 cm is 30 cm 2. Find the length of the arc of the sector.

 Given: Radius (r) =15 cm,

 area of sector = 30 cm 2

 To find: Length of the arc (l).

 Solution:

![Image 1: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 7 Mensuration Practice Set 7.3 1](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-7-Mensuration-Practice-Set-7.3-1.png?resize=350%2C131&ssl=1)

 ∴ The length of the arc is 4 cm.

Practice Set 7.3 Question 6.

 In the adjoining figure, radius of the circle is 7 cm and m (arc MBN) = 60°, find

 i. Area of the circle.

 ii. A(O-MBN).

 iii. A(O-MCN).

![Image 2: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 7 Mensuration Practice Set 7.3 2](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-7-Mensuration-Practice-Set-7.3-2.png?resize=152%2C170&ssl=1)

 Given: radius (r) = 7 cm,

 m(arc MBN) = θ = 60°

 Solution:

 i. Area of circle = πr 2

 = \(\frac { 22 }{ 7 } \) × (7)2

 = 22 × 7

 = 154 cm 2

 ∴ The area of the circle is 154 cm 2

ii. Central angle (θ) = ∠MON = 60°

 Area of sector = \(\frac{\theta}{360} \times \pi r^{2}\)

 ∴ A(O – MBN) = \(\frac { 60 }{ 360 } \) × \(\frac { 22 }{ 7 } \) × (7)2

 \(\frac { 1 }{ 6 } \) × 22 × 7

 = 25.67 cm 2

 = 25.7 cm 2

 ∴ A(O-MBN) = 25.7 cm 2

iii. Area of major sector = area of circle – area of minor sector

 ∴ A(O-MCN) = Area of circle – A(O-MBN)

 = 154 – 25.7

 ∴ A(O-MCN) = 128.3 cm 2

Question 7.

 In the adjoining figure, radius of circle is 3.4 cm and perimeter of sector P-ABC is 12.8 cm. Find A(P-ABC).

 Given: Radius (r) = 3.4 cm,

 perimeter of sector 12.8 cm

 To find: A(P-ABC)

![Image 3: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 7 Mensuration Practice Set 7.3 3](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-7-Mensuration-Practice-Set-7.3-3.png?resize=144%2C156&ssl=1)

 Solution:

 Perimeter of sector

 = Iength of arc ABC + AP + CP

![Image 4: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 7 Mensuration Practice Set 7.3](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-7-Mensuration-Practice-Set-7.3-28.jpg?resize=138%2C162&ssl=1)

 ∴ 12.8 = l + 3.4 + 3.4

 ∴ 12.8 = l + 6.8

 ∴ l = 12.8 – 6.8 = 6cm

![Image 5: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 7 Mensuration Practice Set 7.3 4](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-7-Mensuration-Practice-Set-7.3-4.png?resize=276%2C109&ssl=1)

 ∴ A(P-ABC) = 10.2 cm 2

7.3 Class 10 Question 8.

 In the adjoining figure, O is the centre of the sector. ∠ROQ = ∠MON = 60°. OR = 7 cm, and OM = 21 cm. Find the lengths of arc RXQ and (π = \(\frac { 22 }{ 7 } \))

![Image 6: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 7 Mensuration Practice Set 7.3](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-7-Mensuration-Practice-Set-7.3-29.jpg?resize=157%2C157&ssl=1)

 Given: ∠ROQ = ∠MON = 60°,

 radius (r) = OR = 7 cm, radius (R) = OM = 21 cm

 To find: Lengths of arc RXQ and arc MYN.

 Solution:

 i. Length of arc RXQ = \(\frac{\theta}{360} \times 2 \pi r\)

 = \(\frac { 60 }{ 2 } \) × 2 × \(\frac { 22 }{ 7 } \) × 7

 = \(\frac { 1 }{ 6 } \) × 2 × 22

 = 7.33 cm

 ii. Length of arc MYN = \(\frac{\theta}{360} \times 2 \pi R\)

 = \(\frac { 60 }{ 2 } \) × 2 × \(\frac { 22 }{ 7 } \) × 21

 = \(\frac { 1 }{ 6 } \) × 2 × 22 × 3

 = 22 cm

 ∴ The lengths of arc RXQ and arc MYN are 7.33 cm and 22 cm respectively.

Question 9.

 In the adjoining figure, if A(P-ABC) = 154 cm 2, radius of the circle is 14 cm, find

 i. ∠APC,

 ii. l(arc ABC).

![Image 7: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 7 Mensuration Practice Set 7.3 5](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-7-Mensuration-Practice-Set-7.3-5.png?resize=171%2C165&ssl=1)

 Given: A(P – ABC) = 154 cm 2,

 radius (r) = 14 cm

 Solution:

 i. Let ∠APC = θ

![Image 8: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 7 Mensuration Practice Set 7.3 6](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-7-Mensuration-Practice-Set-7.3-6.png?resize=323%2C90&ssl=1)

![Image 9: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 7 Mensuration Practice Set 7.3 7](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-7-Mensuration-Practice-Set-7.3-7.png?resize=382%2C299&ssl=1)

Std 10 Geometry Mensuration Question 10.

 Radius of a sector of a circle is 7 cm. If measure of arc of the sector is

 i. 30°

 ii. 210°

 iii. three right angles, find the area of the sector in each case.

 Given: Radius (r) = 7 cm

 To find: Area of the sector.

 Solution:

 i. Measure of the arc (θ) = 30°

![Image 10: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 7 Mensuration Practice Set 7.3 8](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-7-Mensuration-Practice-Set-7.3-8.png?resize=254%2C153&ssl=1)

 ∴ Area of the sector is 12.83 cm 2.

 ii. Measure of the arc (θ) = 210°

![Image 11: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 7 Mensuration Practice Set 7.3 9](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-7-Mensuration-Practice-Set-7.3-9.png?resize=255%2C151&ssl=1)

 ∴ Area of the sector is 89.83 cm 2.

 iii. Measure of the arc (θ) = 3 right angle

 = 3 × 90° = 270°

![Image 12: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 7 Mensuration Practice Set 7.3 10](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-7-Mensuration-Practice-Set-7.3-10.png?resize=265%2C156&ssl=1)

 ∴ Area of the sector is 115.50 cm 2.

Mensuration Practice Question 11.

 The area of a minor sector of a circle is 3.85 cm 2 and the measure of its central angle is 36°. Find the radius of the circle.

 Given: Area of minor sector = 3.85 cm 2,

 central angle (θ) = 36°

 To find: Radius of the circle (r).

 Solution:

 Area of minor sector = \(\frac{\theta}{360} \times \pi r^{2}\)

![Image 13: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 7 Mensuration Practice Set 7.3 11](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-7-Mensuration-Practice-Set-7.3-11.png?resize=381%2C397&ssl=1)

 ∴ The radius of the circle ¡s 3.5 cm.

10th Geometry Practice Set 7.3 Question 12.

 In the given figure, ꠸PQRS is a rectangle. If PQ = 14 cm, QR = 21 cm, find the areas of the parts x, y and z.

![Image 14: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 7 Mensuration Practice Set 7.3 12](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-7-Mensuration-Practice-Set-7.3-12.png?resize=196%2C122&ssl=1)

 Given: In rectangle PQRS,

 PQ = 14 cm, QR = 21 cm

 To find: Areas of the parts x, y and z.

 Solution:

![Image 15: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 7 Mensuration Practice Set 7.3 13](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-7-Mensuration-Practice-Set-7.3-13.png?resize=217%2C141&ssl=1)

 ∠Q = ∠R = θ = 90° …[Angles of a rectangle]

![Image 16: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 7 Mensuration Practice Set 7.3 14](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-7-Mensuration-Practice-Set-7.3-14.png?resize=353%2C260&ssl=1)

 For the sector (Q – PA),

 PQ = QA …[Radii of the same circle]

 ∴ QA = 14 cm

 Now, QR = QA + AR … [Q – A – R]

 ∴ 21 = 14 + AR

 ∴ AR = 7 cm

![Image 17: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 7 Mensuration Practice Set 7.3 15](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-7-Mensuration-Practice-Set-7.3-15.png?resize=338%2C281&ssl=1)

 Area of rectangle = length × breadth

 area of ꠸PQRS = PQ × QR

 = 14 × 21

 = 294 cm 2

 Area of part z = area of ꠸PQRS

 – area of part x – area of part y

 = 294 – 154 – 38.5

 = 101.5 cm 2

 ∴ The area of part x is 154 cm 2, the area of part y is 38,5 cm 2 and the area of part z is 101.5 cm 2.

Question 13.

 ∆ALMN is an equilat triangle. LM = 14 cm. As shown in figure, three sectors are drawn with vertices as centres and radius 7 cm. Find,

![Image 18: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 7 Mensuration Practice Set 7.3 16](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-7-Mensuration-Practice-Set-7.3-16.png?resize=186%2C161&ssl=1)

 i. A (∆ LMN).

 ii. Area of any one of the sectors.

 iii. Total area of all the three sectors.

 iv. Area of the shaded region. (\(\sqrt { 3 }\) = 1.732 )

 Given: In equilateral triangle LMN, LM =14 cm,

 radius of sectors (r) = 7 cm

 Solution:

 i. ∆LMN is an equilateral triangle.

### Class 10 Maths Part 2 Practice Set 7.4 Chapter 7 Mensuration Questions With Answers Maharashtra Board

Practice Set 7.4 Geometry Class 10 Question 1. In the adjoining figure, A is the centre of the circle. ∠ABC = 45° and AC = 7 2–√ cm. Find the area of segment BXC, (π = 3.14)

![Image 3: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 7 Mensuration Practice Set 7.4 1](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-7-Mensuration-Practice-Set-7.4-1.png?resize=129%2C152&ssl=1)

 Solution:

 In ∆ABC,

 AC = AB … [Radii of same circle]

 ∴ ∠ABC = ∠ACB …[Isosceles triangle theorem]

 ∴ ∠ABC = ∠ACB = 45°

 In ∆ABC,

 ∠ABC + ∠ACB + ∠BAC = 180° … [Sum of the measures of angles of a triangle is 180° ]

 ∴ 45° + 45° + ∠BAC = 180°

 ∴ 90° + ∠BAC = 180°

 ∴ ∠BAC = 90°

 Let ∠BAC = θ = 90°

![Image 4: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 7 Mensuration Practice Set 7.4 2](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-7-Mensuration-Practice-Set-7.4-2.png?resize=354%2C250&ssl=1)

 Given: m(arc PQR) = 60°, radius (r) = OP = 10 cm

 To find: Area of shaded region.

 ∴ ∠POR = θ = 60°

![Image 6: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 7 Mensuration Practice Set 7.4 4](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-7-Mensuration-Practice-Set-7.4-4.png?resize=336%2C254&ssl=1)

Chapter 7 Maths Class 10 Question 4. In the adjoining figure, if O is the centre of the circle, PQ is a chord, ∠POQ = 90°, area of shaded region is 114 cm2, find the radius of the circle, (π = 3.14)

![Image 10: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 7 Mensuration Practice Set 7.4 8](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-7-Mensuration-Practice-Set-7.4-8.png?resize=147%2C148&ssl=1)

 Given: Central angle (θ) = ∠POQ= 90°,

 A (segment PRQ) = 114 cm 2

 To find: Radius (r).

 …[Taking square root of both sides]

 ∴ r = 20 cm

Mensuration Questions for Class 10 Question 5. A chord PQ of a circle with radius 15 cm subtends an angle of 60° with the centre of the circle. Find the area of the minor as well as the major segment. (π = 3.14, 3–√ = 1.73)

 Given: Radius (r) =15 cm, central angle (θ) = 60°

 To find: Areas of major and minor segments.

 Solution:

 Let chord PQ subtend ∠POQ = 60° at centre.

 ∴ θ = 60°

![Image 12: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 7 Mensuration Practice Set 7.4 10](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-7-Mensuration-Practice-Set-7.4-10.png?resize=346%2C378&ssl=1)

 = 225 [0.0908]

 = 20.43 cm 2

 ∴ area of minor segment = 20.43 cm 2

 Area of circle = πr 2

 = 3.14 × 15 × 15

 = 3.14 × 225

 = 706.5 cm 2

 Area of major segment

 = Area of circle – area of minor segment

 = 706.5 – 20.43

 = 686.07 cm 2

 Area of major segment 686.07 cm 2

 ∴ The area of minor segment Is 20.43 cm 2 and the area of major segment is 686.07 cm 2.

Problem Set 7 Geometry Class 10 Question 2. A washing tub in the shape of a frustum of a cone has height 21 cm. The radii of the circular top and bottom are 20 cm and 15 cm respectively. What is the capacity of the tub? = (π = 22 7)

 Given: For the frustum shaped tub,

 height (h) = 21 cm,

 radii (r 1) = 20 cm, and (r 2) = 15 cm

 To find: Capacity (volume) of the tub.

 Solution:

 Volume of frustum = 1 3 πh (r 1 2 + r 2 2 + r 1 × r 2)

10th Geometry Problem Set 7 Question 3. Some plastic balls of radius 1 cm were melted and cast into a tube. The thickness, length and outer radius of the tube were 2 cm, 90 cm and 30 cm respectively. How many balls were melted to make the tube?

 Given: For the cylindrical tube,

 height (h) = 90 cm,

 outer radius (R) = 30 cm,

 thickness = 2 cm

 For the plastic spherical ball,

 radius (r 1) = 1 cm

 To find: Number of balls melted.

 Solution:

![Image 10: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 7 Mensuration Problem Set 7 8](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-7-Mensuration-Problem-Set-7-8.png?resize=150%2C202&ssl=1)

 Inner radius of tube (r)

 = outer radius – thickness of tube

 = 30 – 2

 = 28 cm

 Volume of plastic required for the tube = Outer volume of tube – Inner volume of hollow tube

 = πR 2 h – πr 2 h

 = πh(R 2 – r 2)

 = π × 90 (30 2 – 28 2)

 = π × 90 (30 + 28) (30 – 28) …[∵ a 2 – b 2 = (a + b)(a – b)]

 = 90 × 58 × 2π cm 3

![Image 11: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 7 Mensuration Problem Set 7 9](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-7-Mensuration-Problem-Set-7-9.png?resize=367%2C353&ssl=1)

 ∴ 7830 plastic balls were melted to make the tube.

Mensuration Problem Question 5. The diameter and length of a roller is 120 cm and 84 cm respectively. To level the ground, 200 rotations of the roller are required. Find the expenditure to level the ground at the rate of ₹ 10 per sq.m.

 Given: For the cylindrical roller,

 diameter (d) =120 cm,

 Rate of levelling = ₹ 10 per m 2

 ∴ Expenditure of levelling the ground

 = 633.6 × 10 = ₹ 6336

 ∴ The expenditure of levelling the ground is ₹ 6336.

Question 6.

 The diameter and thickness of a hollow metal sphere are 12 cm and 0.01 m respectively. The density of the metal is 8.88 gm per cm3. Find the outer surface area and mass of the sphere, [π = 3.14]

 Given: For the hollow sphere,

 diameter (D) =12 cm, thickness = 0.01 m

 density of the metal = 8.88 gm per cm 3

 To find: i. Outer surface area of the sphere

 ii. Mass of the sphere.

 = 4 × 3.14 × 6 2

 = 452.16 cm 2

 Thickness of sphere = 0.01 m

 = 0.01 × 100 cm …[∵ 1 m = 100 cm]

 = 1 cm

 ∴ Inner radius of the sphere (r)

 = Outer radius – thickness of sphere

![Image 15: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 7 Mensuration Problem Set 7 13](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-7-Mensuration-Problem-Set-7-13.png?resize=377%2C381&ssl=1)

Question 10.

 In the adjoining figure, seg AB is a chord of a circle with centre P. If PA = 8 cm and distance of chord AB from the centre P is 4 cm, find the area of the shaded portion.

 (π = 3.14, 3–√ = 1.73)

 = radius of sector C-BXD = [20] cm

 Radius of bigger sector

 = 2–√ × side

 = Area of sector A-PCQ – Area of square ABCD

 = A(A – PCQ) – A(꠸ABCD)

Question 12.

 In the adjoining figure, two circles with centres O and P are touching internally at point A. If BQ = 9, DE = 5, complete the following activity to find the radii of the circles.

![Image 29: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 7 Mensuration Problem Set 7 26](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-7-Mensuration-Problem-Set-7-26.png?resize=163%2C161&ssl=1)

 Solution:

 Let the radius of the bigger circle be R and that of smaller circle be r.

 OA, OB, OC and OD are the radii of the bigger circle.

 ∴ OA = OB = OC = OD = R

 PQ = PA = r

 OQ + BQ = OB … [B – Q – O]

 OQ = OB – BQ = R – 9

 OE + DE = OD ….[D – E – O]

 OE = OD – DE = [R – 5]

 As the chords QA and EF of the circle with centre P intersect in the interior of the circle, so by the property of internal division of two chords of a circle,

 OQ × OA = OE × OF

 ∴ (R – 9) × R = (R – 5) × (R – 5) …[∵ OE = OF]

 ∴ R 2 – 9R = R 2 – 10R + 25

 ∴ -9R + 10R = 25

 ∴ R = [25units]

 AQ = AB – BQ = 2r ….[B-Q-A]

 ∴ 2r = 50 – 9 = 41

 ∴ r = 41 2 = 20.5 units
